prompts.title: Ravel
prompts.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: standalone landscape driving-view environment concept for VECTOR//NOVA, an antigravity racing game.
Style/medium: high-end grounded 3D game environment concept, physically convincing geometry and materials, crisp readable forms at driving speed, cinematic light without painterly blur.
Composition/framing: one continuous widescreen 16:9 image, slightly elevated close chase camera behind one small low-slung antigravity racing craft, showing its full hull in the lower foreground and a broad clear drivable surface leading deep into the environment. Moderate wide-angle perspective, not an aerial establishing shot.
Craft: slender split nose, swept angular pearl ceramic panels over graphite and titanium, dark canopy, restrained vermilion markings, compact powerful blue ion exhaust at real aft nozzles. This is a hovering racing craft, no wheels or helicopter rotors.
Constraints: make the road and its signature interaction immediately understandable through physical form. Real edge thickness, coherent scale, clear receiving surfaces and open racing sightlines. No HUD, no captions, no logos, no typography, no watermarks, no collage or inset panels.
Primary request: RAVEL, a race course on an enormous silver solar sail suspended between distant spacecraft. The environment and the driving surface are the same tensioned fabric structure.
Scene/backdrop: deep space, sparse sharp stars, distant immense cable anchor assemblies and the curve of the sail disappearing into shadow. A low off-axis sun backlights thin foil.
Unique materials: vast silver translucent foil panels, fine woven reinforcement, dark structural fibre seams, purposeful stitched joins, thick cable attachments. Warm champagne transmitted light with cool silver reflections; large folds and broad negative space carry the composition.
Signature mechanic visible in this single frame: the raceable silver membrane rises into a broad smooth traveling wave immediately ahead of the craft, its illuminated crest curling diagonally across the route. Heavy reinforced seams stay flatter and offer a readable stable line. Farther ahead the surface banks up a deep sail fold toward a clearly visible real tear, with a separate broad receiving sheet beyond. One small distant rival is cresting the wave in a short controlled hop to show scale and the surf interaction.
The sail must feel thin, flexible and stretched under enormous tension, not a metal motorway or a solid mountain. Both wave crest and safe seam are clear. The road remains wide enough for several ships. Preserve visibility of the upcoming route and receiving sheet.

prompts.title: Anchor Narrows
prompts.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: Ravel level development concept for VECTOR//NOVA, an antigravity racing game, before implementation.
Input image 1: project-owned Ravel concept reference for material identity, lighting and craft design. Create a NEW view, do not repeat its sparse composition.
Style/medium: polished physically convincing 3D game environment concept. Thin silver woven solar foil, translucent champagne backlight, charcoal carbon reinforcement, titanium clamp housings and dark space. Convincing layered construction, actual three-dimensional playable geometry.
Craft identity: small pearl ceramic/graphite antigravity racecraft, slender split nose and swept angular wings, dark canopy, vermilion accents, two compact bright blue ion engines, no wheels.
Design refinement: make this feel like a complete circuit built THROUGH a working solar sail installation. The course has climbs, banks, plunges, genuine gaps and recovery space. Clear 38-metre-wide silver membrane racing strip bounded by dark reinforced edge seams; opaque thin foil remains readable. Surround it with large connected pleated sail bays, anchored cable bundles, deep clamp assemblies and service galleries attached to rigid anchor frames. Density comes from the sail's construction and layered spaces, not random props or glowing clutter.
Road mechanic: a broad smooth swell propagates along an otherwise continuous flexible roadway. The sheet's height and slope actually change; a magnetically attached craft follows that shape at a low constant hover gap. Strongly tensioned outer seam stays comparatively flat and offers the forgiving line. This is cloth deformation, not liquid, lava, waves drawn on a flat texture, or terrain randomly breaking apart.
Keep all cables and scenery out of the actual racing/camera corridor. No HUD, logos or watermark.
Primary request: show ANCHOR NARROWS, a much richer driving-height image of Ravel that solves the original image's sparseness.
Composition/framing: single widescreen landscape 16:9 image, close readable third-person chase view. The player craft occupies no more than the bottom fifth of the frame; the course and its surroundings dominate.
Track staging: start on a descending foil strip running beside a gigantic curved titanium/carbon anchor buttress. Directly ahead, a broad low swell lifts the middle of the silver roadway into a clear smooth ramp, while its outboard charcoal seam stays low. A small rival rides the swell and the player is on the flatter seam, making both lines understandable. The curve then threads through a tall triangular slot between anchored pleated sail panels and banks steeply upward on a second sheet visible beyond it.
Environment density: a near carbon anchor root and cable clevis frame one edge; overlapping translucent sail folds create substantial middle-distance walls and an overhead canopy with daylight openings. A connected crescent anchor ring, reel machinery and maintenance galleries reveal depth behind the course, with further banked track visible through gaps. Rich broad surfaces and readable layered silhouettes across the whole view, not a few distant towers on an empty plain.
Lighting: warm sun transmits through upper foil, cooler silver light reveals road folds and dark mechanical cavities. Maintain clear separation of upcoming road, player and scenery. The full wave is visible before commitment; do not hide it behind a crest or a huge ship.
No text or explanatory arrows. No concrete/asphalt motorway, no ocean barrel waves, no evenly repeated poles or floating disconnected ornaments.

Primary request: show CROWN FOLD, a wider view revealing how a complete dramatic Ravel track fits within the solar-sail megastructure.
Composition/framing: one landscape 16:9 image, moderately elevated three-quarter environment view near track level, looking diagonally across three connected playable sections at different heights. Not a flat overhead map. Two tiny antigravity craft establish scale without dominating.
Track staging: the near 38-metre-wide silver foil raceway dives into a deep taut fabric valley between dark edge seams, then climbs its banked side into an unmistakable twisting half-roll around a colossal crescent-shaped anchor spine. In the middle distance it emerges onto a short rigid clamp deck and jumps a real open seam onto a broad lower receiving membrane. Beyond that landing, the course sweeps across the installation toward another deeply pleated sail bay. Make the connections, jump and receiver geometrically clear. Prefer three strong large spatial moves over a confusing rollercoaster spaghetti.
Changing surface: show one small local traveling swell crossing the near membrane bay, with the distant receiving bay comparatively taut. The rest of the circuit's large folds and anchor spine remain fixed, so the moving feature reads as a specific local challenge.
Surroundings: layered enormous silver/champagne sail panels form canyons and arches; connected graphite trusses, reeving drums, thick cable fans and staggered maintenance terraces provide mass, recesses and scale. Show underside ribs only at rigid clamp decks. The flexible route itself retains thin woven edges and stretched foil surfaces. Dark open-space apertures separate connected structures.
Lighting: low warm sun grazing silver foil, cool shaded anchor interiors, restrained distant stars. Material variety and bold near/middle/far depth.
No typography, HUD or arrows. No terrain mountains, no bare empty sheet, no city buildings placed on flimsy cloth. Keep all track passages wide and visibly clear.
